comment: Defects found in this repository's own skills and installer.

bugs.title: The shipped core library lost plan_stat_mode and plan_stat_uid, so an installed skill could not read a file mode
bugs.observed: 0 definitions. Two tests said so: test-portable-helpers.sh reported plan_stat_mode: command not found for three assertions, and test-duplication-ratchet.sh reported it is referenced by MAINTAINER.md section 3 but no longer exists.
bugs.expected: Both helpers present in the compiled library; plan_atomic_write calls plan_stat_mode to preserve a file mode.
bugs.mechanism: The re-marking script kept PACKAGE: DEV on any path matching *probe* -- intended for a planted test fixture named plan_probe_dev_only.sh -- and planning/scripts/lib/core/plan_stat_probe.sh matched on its name. PACKAGE: DEV means dev-build-only, so the prod build excluded it.
bugs.fix: Marked plan_stat_probe.sh PACKAGE: PROD and rebuilt. Every other compiler input was checked for the same mistake; it was the only one.
bugs.verification: test-portable-helpers.sh and test-duplication-ratchet.sh both pass; five stat-helper definitions and calls are back in plan-core-lib.sh. Re-marking the file PACKAGE: DEV reproduces the failure.
bugs.found_by: the both-shell run of the release commit, on both bash 5.3 and 3.2
bugs.notes: A name-substring match standing in for a marker. The marker was right in every file; the script that wrote it guessed from the filename. It also shows the release checks were not sufficient on their own: build-release.sh --list and a by-hand diff of npm pack both passed a library with a function missing, because they compare file sets and not file contents.

bugs.title: A second --skill silently discards the first, so the installer installs something other than what was asked
bugs.observed: Selected skills: bug-report — and only bug-report is installed. Reversing the two flags installs only todo. No warning either way.
bugs.expected: Both skills installed, or a refusal naming the conflict. Discarding an argument the caller supplied is the one thing it must not do silently.
bugs.mechanism: installer/src/10-cli-args.sh:60 assigns SKILL_SELECTION="$2" as a scalar, so each --skill overwrites the previous. --all takes the array path; --skill never did.
bugs.verification: README.md:133-135 documents it: "--skill takes one selection... Repeating the flag does not accumulate; the last one wins", and --skill todo,bug-report installs both. Verified: Selected skills: todo bug-report, both directories written. The behaviour matches its documentation, so it is not a defect.
bugs.found_by: installing the two register skills for the user in one command
bugs.notes: Recorded from the install itself without reading the flag documentation first. The residual objection -- that silently discarding a supplied argument is worse than refusing it -- is a design preference, not a defect, and belongs in TODO.json.
